name: South Africa
summary: The Union of South Africa (1910), a republic from 1961. Apartheid laws (1948–1994) enforced racial segregation until the first free elections elected Nelson Mandela in 1994.

knownFor.label: Nelson Mandela
knownFor.note: Anti-apartheid leader and first president elected by all.

knownFor.label: Robben Island
knownFor.note: Prison where Mandela was held; a World Heritage Site.

location.value: The southern tip of Africa, with about 2,800 km of coast on the Atlantic and Indian Oceans; about 1.22 million km².

terrain.value: A large, mostly flat interior plateau between 1,000 and 2,100 m high, with lower coastal land.

climate.value: Generally temperate; the Cape has a Mediterranean climate with winter rain.

resources.value: Diamonds (found in 1867) and gold (Witwatersrand, 1886) started a “Mineral Revolution”; mining remains important.

disasters.value: Droughts, such as the Cape Town water crisis of 2018, and floods, such as the KwaZulu-Natal floods of 2022.

urbanisation.value: Johannesburg is the largest city, followed by Cape Town and Durban.

disease.value: About seven million people living with HIV (2015), more than any other country; the government of the time long denied the link between HIV and AIDS.

migration.value: Forced removals under apartheid; migrants from neighbouring countries.

economicBase.value: Mining, finance, telecommunications and other services; mining is still an important part of the economy.

tradeRoutes.value: The ports of Durban and Cape Town, and railways, serve the whole region.

wealth.value: An upper-middle-income country with the most developed economy in Africa, though unequal.

moneyAndTax.value: The rand, named for the Witwatersrand gold fields.

inequality.value: Among the highest inequality in the world.

keyRulers.value: Jan Smuts; F. W. de Klerk; Nelson Mandela. Later and present leaders are not named here.

eliteConflict.value: Competition among parties after 1994, and rivalry within the ruling ANC.

armyAndTech.value: A regional military power, which once built nuclear weapons and gave them up in 1989–91.

majorWars.value: World Wars; the Border War in Namibia and Angola (1966–89).

alliancesRivals.value: International boycotts and sanctions against apartheid; today a member of BRICS, the African Union and the Commonwealth.

inventions.value: The first human-to-human heart transplant (Christiaan Barnard, Cape Town, 1967).

scienceEducation.value: Under apartheid, schooling was unequal and designed to restrict Black South Africans; reforms since 1994 have narrowed some gaps.

openness.value: Isolated by sanctions and sports boycotts under apartheid, and more open since 1994.

communicationTransport.value: Railways and ports, though rail and electricity systems have struggled in recent years.

religion.value: Mostly Christian, with Muslim, Hindu, Jewish and traditional African beliefs.

languageWriting.value: 12 official languages, including Zulu, Xhosa, Afrikaans and English.

artsArchitecture.value: Literature, jazz and kwaito music, rock art and the Apartheid Museum.

socialStructure.value: Apartheid classified people by race (white, coloured, Indian, Black), and its effects are still visible.

sharedIdentity.value: The “Rainbow Nation” idea, named by Desmond Tutu, aims to unite the country’s many groups.

dailyLife.value: Suburban houses and townships; pap (maize porridge), braai.

neighbours.value: Namibia, Botswana, Zimbabwe, Mozambique and Eswatini; it surrounds Lesotho.

ideasReligions.value: Anti-apartheid ideas and the 1996 constitution, which protects human rights, spread worldwide.

colonisation.value: Formed from British colonies and Boer republics.

riseSignals.value: The Union of South Africa (1910) joined the Cape, Natal, Transvaal and Orange River colonies after the Second Boer War.

peakPeriod.value: The first universal elections (1994) ended apartheid; all racial groups now have political representation.

declineSignals.value: Inequality, unemployment and electricity shortages (load-shedding) since 2008.

outcome.value: South Africa continues as an independent republic.
